title: Tesla Model S on Autopilot braked and steered right to avoid a wrong-way driver on Highway 49 in Cabarrus County, North Carolina, before its driver had reacted
summary: Bret Peters's Model S on Autopilot braked and moved right as a wrong-way car came at him on Highway 49 in North Carolina, and TeslaCam recorded the near miss.
account: Before dawn on 27 February 2020, by the Daily Mail's date, Bret Peters was driving his 2020 Tesla Model S on Autopilot. He is a father and a former state trooper. He was on Highway 49 near Cabarrus Arena in Concord, Cabarrus County, North Carolina. A car traveling the wrong way at about 60 miles per hour came toward him in his lane. He wrote on Facebook that he did not see it until after Autopilot hit the brakes and started steering away. TeslaCam footage shows the Tesla moving into the right lane while the oncoming car swerves onto the grassy median. There was no collision. FOX 46 Charlotte first reported the near miss on 5 March 2020 from its own interview with Peters, and it aired his footage. He told the station that he drives the route for an hour each way twice a day. The station places the drive early on a Friday, a day later than the Daily Mail's 27 February. On 8 March 2020 CleanTechnica relayed a since-deleted Reddit post and the station's report. On 9 March 2020 Electrek and the Daily Mail described the footage. No police or Tesla statement is reported.
purpose: Autopilot is a driver-assistance system that steers, accelerates and brakes within a lane and includes collision-avoidance features. Braking and moving away from an oncoming vehicle is within that intended use as the driver describes it.
system: Tesla Autopilot on a 2020 Model S, with TeslaCam dashcam recording
model_version: 2020 Tesla Model S per the Daily Mail; Autopilot software version not reported

ratings.reason: By his account and the footage as described, one driver was moved out of a wrong-way car's path at about 60 mph before he reacted. The other driver also swerved onto the median, so whether a collision would have occurred is unknown. No avoided injury or damage can be measured.

ai_role.statement: By Peters's account Autopilot braked and began a lane change to the right before he had seen the oncoming car. The TeslaCam footage, as described by Electrek and the Daily Mail, shows the Tesla moving right while the wrong-way car veers off-road. The claim rests on the driver's statements and the footage. Neither Tesla nor police is quoted, and the oncoming driver's own swerve means the system's action cannot be shown to have been decisive.

fields.headline: Tesla Autopilot brakes and steers clear of a wrong-way driver

fields.account: Before dawn on 27 February 2020, by the Daily Mail's date, Bret Peters was driving his 2020 Tesla Model S on Autopilot. He is a father and a former state trooper. He was on Highway 49 near Cabarrus Arena in Concord, Cabarrus County, North Carolina. A car traveling the wrong way at about 60 miles per hour came toward him in his lane. He wrote on Facebook that he did not see it until after Autopilot hit the brakes and started steering away. TeslaCam footage shows the Tesla moving into the right lane while the oncoming car swerves onto the grassy median. There was no collision. FOX 46 Charlotte first reported the near miss on 5 March 2020 from its own interview with Peters, and it aired his footage. He told the station that he drives the route for an hour each way twice a day. The station places the drive early on a Friday, a day later than the Daily Mail's 27 February. On 8 March 2020 CleanTechnica relayed a since-deleted Reddit post and the station's report. On 9 March 2020 Electrek and the Daily Mail described the footage. No police or Tesla statement is reported.

produced_by: Autopilot engaged on a divided highway at night, with an adjacent lane the system has registered as empty
